home.title: Home

empty.title: Add your server
empty.body: Commy connects only to your servers — it has none of its own and never will. Your provider gives you a subscription link, a QR code or a file.
empty.clipboardFound: A link was found in the clipboard

search.nothingBody: No name, address or country code matched.

home.ipCheckFailed: Access confirmed, $ms ms, the IP check did not answer
home.switchedToAuto: The server is now chosen automatically
home.failedOver: The server stopped answering — switched to $name

measureSkippedUdp(plural, param=count).one: $count UDP server cannot be timed over TCP — pick GET or ICMP under Ping
measureSkippedUdp(plural, param=count).other: $count UDP servers cannot be timed over TCP — pick GET or ICMP under Ping

subscription.title: Subscription URL
subscription.subtitle: Server list, quota and expiry from your panel
subscription.name: Name (optional)
subscription.invalidUrl: That does not look like an http or https link

qr.title: Scan a QR code
qr.permissionBody: Asked for here only, and only while the scanner is open.
qr.batchHint: Scan the codes one after another; they are all added at once.

file.title: Open a config file
file.subtitle: sing-box JSON, Clash YAML, base64
file.unreadable: The file could not be read

result.nothingBody: Check that the text holds a vless:// style link or a base64 subscription.
result.alreadyThere: You already had this subscription — it was refreshed in place.
result.batchFailed: Subscriptions that could not be added: $count. The log says why.

skippedReason.notALink: Not a server, nor a link to one
skippedReason.unsupportedUnnamed: The server needs something Commy does not have
skippedReason.incomplete: Something required is missing: the address, port, key or password
skippedReason.unknownFormat: Not a link list, a Clash file or a sing-box config
skippedReason.encrypted: An encrypted $app link: only $app can open it. Ask your provider for the plain subscription address (https://…)
skippedReason.encryptedUnnamed: An encrypted link: only the app it was made for can open it. Ask your provider for the plain subscription address (https://…)

routing.title: Routing profile
routing.note: The profile replaces your routing rules. The current rules stay as a profile of their own — you can switch back any time.
routing.invalid: This routing-profile link is damaged or from a newer Commy

subscription.title: Subscription

changeLink.title: New link
changeLink.body: If the panel gave you a new link, paste it here. The card, its interval, its User-Agent and the chosen server stay; the servers are fetched again from the new link.
changeLink.invalid: This needs a link that starts with http:// or https://

userAgent.title: User-Agent
userAgent.body: How the app introduces itself to the panel. Some panels answer each client differently: if servers are missing or the subscription will not load, pick a client the panel knows.
userAgent.invalid: Latin letters, digits and punctuation only

interval.title: Refresh interval
interval.body: How often the app re-downloads the subscription while auto refresh is on.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this subscription?
deleteConfirm.body: Its servers and their credentials go with it. The link itself can be added again.

subscription.refreshBusy: Another subscription is refreshing — try this one again in a moment
subscription.panelSaid: Your panel sent this instead of servers:
subscription.deviceIdOff: Sending the device identifier (HWID) is off, and a panel that limits devices answers like this without it.
subscription.noServers: This subscription has no servers yet

recovery.title: Address recovery
recovery.statusPoint: Provider key pinned, mirrors: $mirrors, checked at: $host
recovery.off: Off: if the address is blocked, the subscription will not move by itself
recovery.changedHint: If you did not expect a move, do not trust it and ask your provider.
recovery.viaMirror: The main address did not answer; updated through a mirror

node.noLink: This protocol has no share link format

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this server?
deleteConfirm.body: Its credentials go with it. A server that came from a subscription comes back on the next refresh.
deleteConfirm.inUse: The tunnel is running through this server and will be disconnected.

ruleSets.title: Rule sets
ruleSets.intro: A rule naming geosite: or geoip: needs a compiled list on disk. Nothing is downloaded until you ask — with the button or a schedule. The address below is the one that will be asked.
ruleSets.sourceHelp: $token is replaced with the tag being fetched, $kind with geoip or geosite. Clear the field to make downloading unavailable.
ruleSets.sourceInvalid: That does not look like an http or https address
ruleSets.noneNeededBody: Rules naming geosite: or geoip: are the ones that do. Plain domains and addresses work without anything downloaded.
ruleSets.autoUpdateHint: Only sets already downloaded and used by your rules, from the same source
ruleSets.autoUpdateBody: Commy fetches them again on this schedule — only the ones already on the phone and used by your rules, from the same address as the button. Off — only when you tap Update.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this list?
deleteConfirm.body: The rules that name it stay where they are and stop applying until it is downloaded again.

apps.title: Apps
apps.modeDisabledHint: Every app goes through the tunnel. The list below is kept but not applied.
apps.modeIncludeHint: Only the apps you tick go through the tunnel. Everything else goes out directly.
apps.modeExcludeHint: Every app goes through the tunnel except the ones you tick.
apps.selfHint: Always outside the tunnel: an app that fetched its own subscription through its own tunnel could never recover from a bad one.
apps.empty: This platform does not route by app
apps.emptyBody: Per-app routing is an Android feature. On the desktops every app uses the tunnel.
apps.nothingFoundBody: Try part of the name, or the package.
apps.hiddenBySystemBody: Everything matching this search is a system app, and those are hidden by the switch above.

dns.title: DNS
dns.remoteHint: Answers for names that go through the proxy, and is asked through it
dns.directHint: Answers for names that bypass the proxy
dns.footer: Two resolvers, always. One asked through the tunnel and one asked outside it is the whole reason a DNS query cannot say where you are; a single resolver for both is the classic leak.
dns.fakeIpHint: Answers from a private pool instead of resolving. Faster, and no real address reaches the system cache.
dns.independentCacheHint: One cache per resolver. Shared, two answers to the same name overwrite each other.

edit.label: Resolver
edit.help: Schemes: $schemes. A bare address means plain UDP. "local" hands the query to the system.
edit.helpRemote: Schemes: $schemes. A bare address means plain UDP.
edit.unsupportedScheme: The core has no transport for that scheme
edit.missingAddress: There is no address after the scheme
edit.systemThroughTunnel: The system resolver answers outside the tunnel: every name going through the proxy would leak. Give a resolver address

qr.nodeCaption: Scan it in another client to add this server.
qr.subscriptionCaption: Scan it in another client to add this subscription.
qr.subscriptionWarning: Anyone who scans this gets your subscription link, and with it every server on it. Show it only to a device you own.
qr.tooLong: This one is too long to scan. Copy the link instead.

silence.title: Silence on the wire
silence.body: Not one outgoing request you did not ask for. Below is the complete list of exceptions, and it is closed.
silence.blockListsMissing: on, but the list is not downloaded — open Rule sets
silence.recoveryHint: when the address is silent and once a day, with no identifiers
silence.footer: No new exception can appear without changing this screen.

identity.title: Device identifier
identity.sendHint: Only to your subscription's host. Panels that limit devices answer without it with a placeholder instead of servers. It is a random number for this install, not your phone's serial.
identity.resetHint: The panel will see a new device

connection.title: Connection
connection.startOnBootHint: A notification after the phone restarts; one tap on it connects. The tunnel can't come up without the app.
connection.killSwitchHint: Provided by Android: Always-on VPN with "Block connections without VPN". Tap to open it.
connection.killSwitchUnavailable: This system has no VPN settings screen
connection.hideUnavailableHint: Servers that did not answer a probe
connection.failoverHint: If the chosen server stops answering, Commy moves to the fastest live one — from the same subscription first. The tunnel is not dropped

ping.title: Ping
ping.getHint: A request through the server itself: shows whether it really works. Works without connecting too
ping.tcpHint: How fast the server accepts a connection, measured directly. Quick, but does not check that it carries traffic
ping.icmpHint: A plain ping to the server's address. Many servers do not answer it

backup.title: Backup
backup.exportHint: Subscriptions, servers, rules and settings, in one file under a password

password.exportBody: The backup holds your subscriptions and the keys to your servers. Without the password nobody can open it: not whoever gets the file, and not you. A lost password cannot be recovered.
password.label: Password

restoreConfirm.title: Replace everything with the backup?
restoreConfirm.body: Backup of $date: $contents. Subscriptions, servers, rules and settings on this phone will be replaced, and the tunnel disconnects. The device ID (HWID) is not carried over: the panel sees this phone, not the one the backup came from.

backup.ruleSetsMissing: Rule sets are not part of a backup — download them again
backup.perAppDropped: The app list was made on another system — it is turned off

skipped(plural, param=count).one: $count entry of the backup was not read: a newer version made it
skipped(plural, param=count).other: $count entries of the backup were not read: a newer version made them

reset.title: Reset
reset.networkHint: Routing, rules and DNS, as after install

networkConfirm.title: Reset network?
networkConfirm.body: The routing mode, your rules, the app list, ad blocking and DNS settings go back to their defaults. Servers and subscriptions stay. A running tunnel picks up the new settings at once.

reset.appHint: Theme, language, connection and checks, as after install

appConfirm.title: Reset app settings?
appConfirm.body: Theme, text size, language, auto connect, start on boot, checks and the other settings go back to their defaults. Servers, subscriptions, routing and DNS stay.

reset.failed: Could not reset: the store refused the write

routing.title: Routing

inactive.body: These rules are not in force right now: only Rules mode reads them.

routing.finalRuleHint: The last rule is always there and cannot be removed: routing must have a final outcome.

dropped.title: Some rules are not being applied
dropped.body: They name a rule set that is not on disk. The tunnel still comes up, but these rules do nothing until the sets are downloaded.
dropped.bodyGeneric: The tunnel still comes up, but these rules do nothing right now. Each line says why.
dropped.adBlock: Ad blocking — the $tag list is not downloaded
dropped.perAppUnavailable: Per-app routing is not available on this device
dropped.perAppIncludeOnly: “Only these apps” is not available on this device — the list is not applied

newRule.title: New rule
newRule.enabledHint: A rule that is off keeps its place in the list but does nothing
newRule.unknown: Not a condition the app knows. Start it with domain:, suffix:, keyword:, geosite:, geoip:, ip:, port: or app:

routing.emptyRules: No rules of your own yet
routing.emptyRulesBody: With no rules everything follows the final outcome. Add the first one to split the traffic.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.name: Name
profiles.newBody: A new profile is a copy of the current rules. Edit it as usual; switch with a tap on the profile, without reconnecting.
profiles.activeCannotDelete: The active profile cannot be deleted — switch to another first
profiles.failed: The profile could not be saved

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.redactionNotice: UUIDs, passwords and subscription links are stripped automatically when copying and exporting.
diagnostics.logsEmptyBody: The core writes here while the tunnel runs. Connect and the lines will appear.
diagnostics.logsFilteredBody: No line passes the current level and search.
diagnostics.connectionsEmptyBody: This shows which rule matched each host. The list fills up while traffic flows.
diagnostics.configEmptyBody: The configuration appears the moment you connect: it is assembled from the chosen server, the rules and DNS.
diagnostics.configRedacted: Secrets are stripped. This is what goes to the core, minus the credentials.
diagnostics.configNotBuilt: The configuration could not be built
diagnostics.statsEmptyBody: The chart shows the last 60 seconds; the rows below, this session's usage and the last week by day.
diagnostics.statsChart: Traffic over the last 60 seconds, peak $peak

exportWarning.title: Export the logs?
exportWarning.body: Credentials, subscription links and full addresses are stripped before saving. Read the file before sending it anywhere.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.reduceMotionHint: No springs or travelling highlights, only colour changes. The system setting applies either way

about.title: About
about.notAService: Commy is not a VPN service. No servers of ours, no bundled configs, no accounts and no backend.
about.storageDegraded: The database is not encrypted in this build. Secrets still live in the system keystore.

subscriptionUnreachable.message: The subscription server is not answering

subscriptionRefused.message: The panel refused the request: HTTP ${status}. The subscription may be expired, revoked, or over its device limit.

subscriptionServerError.message: The subscription server is having trouble: HTTP ${status}. That is on its side — try again later.

subscriptionCertificate.message: The subscription server's certificate was not accepted: it is expired, self-signed or issued for another name. Check the date and time on this device; if they are right, it is for whoever runs the panel to fix.

subscriptionInsecureRedirect.message: The subscription server redirected to an unencrypted (http) address. Commy does not follow it: the link and the servers would cross the network in the clear.

subscriptionRedirect.message: The subscription server keeps redirecting, or redirects somewhere Commy does not go. Retrying gets the same answer — check the subscription address or ask the panel's support.

subscriptionMalformed.message: The subscription response could not be read

permissionDenied.message: The tunnel cannot come up without VPN permission

helperUnavailable.message: The tunnel service is not running

backup.notABackup: This is not a Commy backup
backup.newerVersion: A newer Commy made this backup — update the app
backup.wrongPassword: The password does not fit — or the file was changed after it was saved
backup.unreadable: The backup is damaged and cannot be read

verdict.worksBody: A request went through the server. If sites still do not open, look at routing and DNS.
verdict.dnsFailed: The server name does not resolve
verdict.dnsFailedBody: A typo in the address, an expired domain, or DNS filtered on this network. Try another network or refresh the subscription.
verdict.portClosedBody: The server is down, or this network or the server firewall blocks the port. Try another server or mobile data.
verdict.tlsFailedBody: The connection drops at the handshake — the usual sign of blocking by name (SNI). Try another server or network.
verdict.certificateRefusedBody: The certificate expired, is for another name, or the phone clock is wrong.
verdict.protocolRefused: The server answers but passes no traffic
verdict.protocolRefusedBody: The network to the server is fine; the protocol is not. Most likely the key expired, the plan ran out, or DPI blocks the protocol. Refresh the subscription or contact your provider.
verdict.reachableBody: The network to the server is fine. The check through the server is off: Ping has no probe address.
